evidence.quote: item_count = sum(qty for _, _, qty in lines)

criteria.reasoning:
render_page sums the third tuple field (qty), which is the same field the existing row template renders as quantity, and writes it into a

as 'Items: N'. The default argument is DEMO_LINES. The unit test passes on the default demo page and asserts the exact fragment 'data-testid="item-count">Items: 5<'. The verifier-generated browser test failed at the merge base and passes at head. That shows the served page shows the count too, not just the function.

test_adequacy.reason: It asserts the exact text 'Items: 5' inside the item-count element of the rendered demo page, which is what the criterion observes. It calls render_page directly rather than going through the served app, but the e2e test covers that.
The verifier generated this browser test. It fails at the base and passes at head, so it checks the item count the page shows end to end.

findings.title: Empty cart shows the count element with zero
findings.detail:
No scenario covers a cart with no lines. In that case sum() over an empty tuple gives 0, so the page renders

Items: 0

. A different implementation could hide the element instead.

evidence.quote: item_count = sum(qty for _, _, qty in lines)

findings.suggested_fix: WHEN the cart page is rendered for a cart with no line items THEN the element with data-testid="item-count" shows `Items: 0`.

findings.title: No singular form for a count of one
findings.detail: For a total quantity of 1 the page shows 'Items: 1' and does not switch to a singular form like 'Item: 1'. The spec only fixes the `Items: N` template, so other implementations could differ here.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN the cart's line quantities sum to 1 THEN the page shows `Items: 1`.

riskiest_assumptions: DEMO_LINES (not shown in the diff) holds exactly 2 × Pen and 3 × Notebook, with quantity as the third tuple element.
The page served by pricing.web.app calls render_page() with the default DEMO_LINES (the passing e2e test supports this).
The gate report's per-test outcomes were produced on the committed head shown in this diff.
